Cluster axis guide for ggplot2

Source: R/guide-axis-cluster.R
guide_axis_cluster.Rd

guide_axis_cluster() draws a hierarchical clustering dendrogram along a discrete x or y axis. The companion scales scale_x_cluster() and scale_y_cluster() cluster the categories themselves, so the categories are re-ordered into dendrogram leaf order and the tree is aligned to the new positions automatically.

Usage

guide_axis_cluster(
  data = NULL,
  method = c("ward.D", "ward.D2", "single", "complete", "average", "mcquitty", "median",
    "centroid"),
  height = 1,
  col = "black",
  lwd = 0.7,
  type = c("rectangle", "triangle"),
  hclust = NULL,
  free = NULL,
  map_data = NULL,
  .tree_labels = NULL,
  cluster_position = NULL,
  show_labels = TRUE,
  draw_tree = TRUE,
  title = ggplot2::waiver(),
  position = ggplot2::waiver(),
  order = 0,
  theme = NULL,
  ...
)

scale_x_cluster(
  data = NULL,
  method = "complete",
  height = 1,
  ring_gap = NULL,
  col = "black",
  lwd = 0.7,
  type = c("rectangle", "triangle"),
  free = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  labels = ggplot2::waiver(),
  limits = NULL,
  expand = ggplot2::waiver(),
  position = "bottom",
  tree_position = NULL,
  strip_side = c("below", "above"),
  name = ggplot2::waiver(),
  guide = NULL,
  value = NULL,
  .map_data = NULL,
  ...
)

scale_y_cluster(
  data = NULL,
  method = "complete",
  height = 1,
  col = "black",
  lwd = 0.7,
  type = c("rectangle", "triangle"),
  free = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  labels = ggplot2::waiver(),
  limits = NULL,
  expand = ggplot2::waiver(),
  position = "left",
  tree_position = NULL,
  strip_side = c("below", "above"),
  name = ggplot2::waiver(),
  guide = NULL,
  value = NULL,
  .map_data = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A numeric matrix or data frame whose rows are the categorical levels to cluster (rownames() give the labels) and whose columns are the features used for clustering. Alternatively an hclust object, or — for scale_x_cluster() / scale_y_cluster() — omitted, in which case the matrix is derived from the plot's own data (see Details).

method

Clustering method passed to stats::hclust(). One of "ward.D", "ward.D2", "single", "complete", "average", "mcquitty", "median" or "centroid".

height

Overall height of the dendrogram, in centimetres. For a cartesian y axis this is the width of the tree. On a coord_radial() theta axis it is the thickness of the ring dendrogram (inwards for position = "bottom", outwards for "top"); for an r-axis tree on a partial arc it is the angular width of the wedge (min(pi/3, 0.30 * height) radians).

col

Colour of the dendrogram lines.

lwd

Line width of the dendrogram lines.

type

Shape of the dendrogram. "rectangle" (the default) draws rectangular branches, like plot.dendrogram(type = "rectangle"). "triangle" draws diagonal branches, like plot.dendrogram(type = "triangle").

hclust

An optional hclust object. When supplied, data and method are ignored. This is used internally by scale_x_cluster() and scale_y_cluster() so that the scale and the guide share one clustering.

free

For use with facet_wrap(scales = "free"). When TRUE, the dendrogram is computed per panel from the subset of data rows that match that panel's categories, so each facet gets its own tree and its own leaf order. When data is omitted (see scale_x_cluster()) the per-panel matrix is rebuilt from the plot data instead, so no matrix is required. See the "Faceted free scales" section below.

map_data

Internal. Long frame (.focal, .other, .value) used to rebuild the matrix of a free-scale panel; filled in automatically by the cluster scales.

.tree_labels

Internal. The raw category names, used to match a tree's leaves when the displayed labels differ from the axis values (free facets re-key them per panel).

cluster_position

Where the tree sits when the guide is attached directly with guides(); defaults to the axis side ("bottom" for an x axis, "left" for a y axis).

show_labels

When FALSE the labels keep their layout but are drawn invisibly, so only the tree shows – used when a secondary axis carries the tree while the main axis prints the category names.

draw_tree

Internal switch used by scale_x_cluster(): FALSE draws only the labels, and the tree is injected into the finished gtable instead (that is what position = "top" needs).

title

Axis title, passed on to ggplot2::guide_axis().

position

Where the dendrogram is drawn: "bottom"/"top" for an x axis, "left"/"right" for a y axis. The category names always stay on the usual side (bottom for x, left for y); position moves the tree only. With "top" the tree is drawn above the panel, and in a facetted plot it is placed between the strip and the panel. On a coord_radial() plot "bottom" puts the x tree inside the hole and "top" outside the circle; the r-axis tree always sits at the label-free end of the arc, so position does not move it (see "Radial coordinates" below).

order, theme

Passed on to ggplot2::guide_axis().

...

Further arguments passed to ggplot2::scale_x_discrete() / ggplot2::scale_y_discrete().

ring_gap

Gap in centimetres between the circle and the leaf ring of a coord_radial() theta-axis dendrogram. The default NULL measures the theta labels and puts the leaf ring right after the longest one; supply a number to override that.

tree_position

Optional alias for position, kept for scripts written before position was redefined to move only the tree.

strip_side

Where the tree sits relative to the facet strip when the tree is on the strip side (an x axis with position = "top"): "below" (the default) slides it between the strip and the panel, "above" puts it outside the strip. Ignored when the tree is not next to a strip.

name, labels, limits, expand, breaks

Arguments passed on to ggplot2::scale_x_discrete() / ggplot2::scale_y_discrete(). By default breaks is the dendrogram leaf order, which is what re-orders the axis.

guide

A guide. By default a matching guide_axis_cluster() is created from the same clustering.

value

Optional column name to cluster on, when the plot maps several numeric aesthetics and the automatic choice (first of fill, colour, size, linewidth, alpha, weight) is not the intended one. Only scale_x_cluster() / scale_y_cluster() use it, because the matrix is derived from the plot data.

.map_data

Internal, same as map_data; kept on the scale signatures so the derived long frame reaches the guide.

Value

guide_axis_cluster() returns a guide object; scale_x_cluster() / scale_y_cluster() return a discrete ggplot2 scale.

Details

The dendrogram is computed with stats::dist() (Euclidean distance) followed by stats::hclust(). Rows containing missing values are dropped with a warning before clustering.

Tree placement

position only decides where the tree is drawn, never where the labels go. The labels always stay on their usual side of the panel, so the tree can sit on the opposite side without moving anything the reader is used to.

  • "bottom" / "top" (x axis): below or above the labels. With facets the tree is moved into the strip band, i.e. directly under the strip and above the panel, so strip, tree, labels and panel never overlap. Use strip_side = "above" to draw it outside the strip instead; either way a small gap (options(ggutils.tree_gap = 0.14), in centimetres) keeps the branches from touching the strip.

  • "left" / "right" (y axis): left of the labels, or at the far end of the panel row. With facets, "left" draws one tree per visible y axis; "right" draws one at the end of every panel row.

A tree that has to sit away from the labels cannot travel through the axis guide (a discrete secondary axis cannot carry a free panel's categories), so it is drawn straight into the finished gtable, where the panel geometry is known. That is also what makes facet_grid() work: the row facet owns the y axis and the column facet owns the x axis, and each tree is attached to the strip of its own cell.

Facets and scales

The scales argument of facet_wrap() / facet_grid() is read automatically, so free never has to be written by hand:

  • "fixed": one shared tree for every panel.

  • "free_x": each panel column gets its own x tree.

  • "free_y": y trees are recomputed per panel row.

  • "free": both axes are recomputed panel by panel.

facet_wrap() draws one x tree per panel row (each under its own strip) and one y tree per visible y axis; facet_grid() draws one x tree per panel and one y tree per row. Writing free = FALSE forces a single shared tree, free = TRUE forces per-panel trees regardless of scales.

Free facets

facet_wrap(scales = "free") gives every panel its own set of categories, and with free = TRUE its own tree. A discrete scale's limits are global, so the categories are re-keyed per panel internally: each panel's focal column becomes "<panel>__ggcl__<category>" and is ordered by that panel's own hclust() leaf order. The axis therefore really is in leaf order, a standard tree can be drawn without a crossing branch, and the prefix never reaches the printed labels. Users never see the keys.

With an explicitly supplied matrix (data = mat) the axis stays in data order and the panel tree falls back to merging only adjacent clusters, which keeps the layout planar at the cost of a shape that differs from a plain hclust().

Deriving the matrix from the plot

scale_x_cluster() and scale_y_cluster() do not need a matrix. When data is omitted, the matrix is built from the plot data at draw time:

  1. the focal axis (x for scale_x_cluster(), y for scale_y_cluster()) provides the rows, the other positional axis provides the columns;

  2. the values come from the first numeric aesthetic mapped among fill, colour, size, linewidth, alpha and weight; use the value argument to pick another column;

  3. with no numeric aesthetic, a continuous other axis is summarised per category (mean, sd, median, n), and two categorical axes are clustered on how often the categories co-occur (a message says so).

ggplot(df, aes(gene, sample, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_x_cluster()                       # no matrix needed

Missing focal/other combinations are filled with the row mean instead of dropping the category, so an incomplete grid still keeps every label on the axis. hclust remains available for a pre-computed tree.

A guide on its own cannot change the order in which a scale maps categories to positions: that order is fixed before the guide is built. Therefore, to both draw the tree and re-order the axis, use scale_x_cluster() / scale_y_cluster(). If you attach guide_axis_cluster() directly with guides(x = ...), the tree is aligned to the categories but the data order is left unchanged.

Radial coordinates (coord_radial())

On a circular plot the theta (x) and r (y) axes are handled differently.

theta axis (x) – ring dendrogram. The category labels keep their stock guide_axis_theta() look and the tree becomes a ring dendrogram: leaves on a circle, every merge an arc at another radius, joined to its children by radial stubs. type = "triangle" draws straight chords to each merge instead of arcs.

  • position = "bottom" (default) draws the tree inside the hole: the leaves sit on the inner circle and every merge steps towards the centre. This needs inner.radius > 0; a pie without a hole has no room, so the tree is skipped.

  • position = "top" draws it outside the circle: leaves on the outer circle, merges growing outwards. With the default ring_gap = NULL the leaf ring starts after the longest theta label, and extra padding is inserted around every panel, so facet strips and neighbouring panels are never touched. Leave some plot.margin / device room for the tree.

r axis (y) – partial arcs only. On a full circle the r axis is a plain column, so scale_y_cluster() draws no tree there. With a partial arc (start/end) ggplot2 puts the r labels on a radial ray and the tree becomes an arc-shaped wedge dendrogram at the other end of the arc, the side without labels: the leaf position becomes a radius and the merge height an angle, so every straight branch becomes a concentric arc and the tree hugs the heat map. height sets the angular width (min(pi/3, 0.30 * height) radians).

Facets. Every panel gets its own tree, and with facet_wrap(scales = "free_x") that tree is clustered from the panel's own genes, so the panels differ. With fixed scales one shared tree is used.

# per-sample z-scores: standardise every sample across the genes once
z <- local({
  m <- tapply(airway_heatmap$df$z,
              list(airway_heatmap$df$gene, airway_heatmap$df$sample), mean)
  m <- scale(m)                                # column-wise = per sample
  out <- as.data.frame(as.table(m))
  names(out) <- c("gene", "sample", "z_sample")
  merge(out, airway_heatmap$genes[c("gene", "gene_set")], by = "gene")
})
d <- droplevels(z[z$gene %in% unique(z$gene)[1:16], ])
fill_scale <- scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166ac", mid = "white",
                                   high = "#b2182b", midpoint = 0,
                                   name = "z (sample)")

# (1) x tree inside the hole: bottom + inner.radius
ggplot(d, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) + geom_tile() +
  coord_radial(theta = "x", inner.radius = 0.55) +
  scale_x_cluster(method = "ward.D2", height = 1.2) +
  fill_scale

# (2) x tree outside the circle: position = "top"
ggplot(d, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) + geom_tile() +
  coord_radial(theta = "x") +
  scale_x_cluster(method = "ward.D2", height = 1, position = "top") +
  fill_scale

# (3) partial arc + r-axis tree at the label-free end of the arc
ggplot(d, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) + geom_tile() +
  coord_radial(theta = "x", start = -0.5 * pi, end = 0.5 * pi,
               inner.radius = 0.55) +
  scale_y_cluster(method = "ward.D2", height = 1.6) +
  fill_scale

# (4) facetted: one tree per panel, clustered per panel
ggplot(d, aes(gene, sample, fill = z_sample)) + geom_tile() +
  facet_wrap(~ gene_set, scales = "free_x") +
  coord_radial(theta = "x", inner.radius = 0.45) +
  scale_x_cluster(method = "ward.D2", height = 0.8) +
  fill_scale +
  theme_grey(base_size = 7)

Faceted free scales

With facet_wrap(scales = "free_x") (or "free_y") every panel has its own categories, so one pre-computed tree cannot fit all panels. In that case pass the clustering data to the guide itself and set free = TRUE:

ggplot(d, aes(gene, value)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ cluster, scales = "free_x") +
  guides(x = guide_axis_cluster(data = mat, free = TRUE, method = "average"))

The guide then takes, in each panel, the rows of mat whose names match that panel's categories, clusters that subset, and draws a tree sized for exactly those leaves. When the matrix was derived from the plot data (no data argument), the per-panel matrix is rebuilt from that long data, so combinations missing from a panel cannot become NA and drop a category. The scale must leave the category order to the data (do not set global limits); if you also want the categories re-ordered per panel, use scale_x_cluster()/scale_y_cluster() with free = TRUE, which re-orders each panel's axis into that panel's leaf order for you.

Canvas height

The tree row is a fixed height (in cm), while panel rows are 1null. When the fixed rows (trees + rotated axis labels + strips) need more room than the device provides, gtable gives the null panel rows zero height and the figure looks like trees and axis text only. Leave roughly 2-3 cm of height per panel row – with two rows of faceted panels plus rotated labels, a fig.height of 4 inches is already too short. Either enlarge the device or lower height.

See also

ggplot2::guide_axis(), ggplot2::scale_x_discrete()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(1)
mat <- matrix(rnorm(12 * 5), nrow = 12,
              dimnames = list(paste0("g", 1:12), paste0("s", 1:5)))
long <- as.data.frame(as.table(mat))
names(long) <- c("gene", "sample", "value")

# x axis: genes are clustered and re-ordered, tree above the labels
ggplot(long, aes(gene, sample, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_x_cluster(mat, method = "average", height = 1.2, col = "#b2182b") +
  scale_y_discrete(guide = guide_axis(show.tick.label = TRUE))

# y axis: same matrix, tree to the right of the labels
ggplot(long, aes(sample, gene, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_y_cluster(mat, method = "ward.D2", height = 1.2, col = "#2166ac")

# No matrix at all: the tree is clustered from the plot data itself
ggplot(long, aes(gene, sample, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_x_cluster(method = "average", position = "top")

# Tree away from the labels: x labels stay at the bottom, the tree moves
# under the strip; y labels stay on the left, the tree moves to the right
ggplot(long, aes(gene, sample, fill = value)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ sample, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_x_cluster(position = "top", height = 1)

ggplot(long, aes(gene, sample, fill = value)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ sample, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_cluster(position = "left", height = 1)

# Both axes at once; `scales` is picked up from the facet
ggplot(long, aes(gene, sample, fill = value)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~ sample, scales = "free") +
  scale_x_cluster(position = "top", height = 1) +
  scale_y_cluster(position = "left", height = 1)

# facet_grid: the row facet owns y, the column facet owns x.
# Group both axes so the grid stays small; drop = FALSE keeps the empty
# levels visible, which is what makes "fixed" and "free_y" differ.
grid_df <- long
grid_df$g_half <- factor(ifelse(grid_df$gene %in% paste0("g", 1:6),
                                "g1-g6", "g7-g12"))
grid_df$s_half <- factor(ifelse(grid_df$sample %in% c("s1", "s2"),
                                "s1-s2", "s3-s5"))
ggplot(grid_df, aes(gene, sample, fill = value)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(s_half ~ g_half, scales = "free", drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_cluster(position = "top", height = 1) +
  scale_y_cluster(position = "left", height = 1)
} # }
